clue.text: After which competitors come out of their shells

definitions.text: After which competitors come out of their shells

parts.words: After which competitors come out of their shells
parts.note: shells are the light racing boats rowers sit in, so this is the event at the end of which crews climb out of them, not hatching creatures

explanation.surface: A riddle about creatures emerging from their shells once a contest is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The University Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames; a racing eight is called a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing contest is one whose crews sit in shells, the slim racing hulls, and step out at the finish.

clue.text: Card in this suit is bare

explanation.surface: A greetings card for an occasion where your outfit is nakedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves need the answer slotted in: a ___ card, and a ___ suit, meaning nakedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards are sent on the anniversary of one's arrival, and the suit of that day is the naked skin one was born in.

clue.text: Order member North-East after start of month

indicators.note: after puts the compass direction behind the start of the month

parts.note: the first of one month is August I, read with the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monk posted to the north-east at the beginning of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of month' is not M but a date: August 1, written with the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar or canon of the religious order named after St Augustine of Hippo.

clue.text: 23 drops by to perform a piece of music

indicators.note: drops means the word by is taken away from the answer to 23

parts.note: the answer to 23 across is the poet's name
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A poet leaves to play a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops by' looks like visiting; it means the answer to 23 across loses BY, leaving RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical form in which a main theme returns between contrasting episodes, often a final movement.

clue.text: Head's measure produces upset

explanation.surface: Measuring your head leads to an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer is the measurement of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats are sold by the size of cap; to overturn a boat is to upset it.

clue.text: Quiet voice in golf club

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet
to voice something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken remark made inside the clubhouse of a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-game club used on the green for rolling the ball towards the hole.

clue.text: Organized workers fail to achieve this standard

parts.note: a union is a body of organized workers
to flag is to tire or fail

explanation.surface: Unionized workers falling short of the required standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality, but it is a banner; the Union Flag is the British national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner, and this is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Delicate stroke in match

explanation.surface: A deft shot played during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A light deft stroke, as of a brush; and to equal or rival, as in 'nobody can come near him'.

clue.text: He skirts round a French city

indicators.note: round says the edges go around the pronoun

parts.note: skirts and rims are both edges or borders
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks around the outskirts of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts round' looks like avoiding something; RIMS goes round HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims, also spelt Reims, is the city in Champagne where French kings were crowned.

clue.text: Pub's bill for wine

parts.note: a pub is a bar, with the possessive s kept
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A pub's bill for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region, near Sauternes.

clue.text: Princess rebuffs half-hearted shrew

indicators.note: rebuffs, read as re-buffs or turns back, says the word for shrew is turned round
half-hearted says one of the pair of letters at the word's heart is lost

parts.note: a shrew is a nagging woman, a nagger

explanation.surface: A princess spurns a scold who lacks real conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' leaves NAGER from NAGGER, the middle GG halved; 'rebuffs' turns that to REGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare, so a princess of Britain in the play.

clue.text: Commonplace liberty taken with front of the paper

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of the word paper

parts.note: latitude is freedom or liberty of action

explanation.surface: A newspaper takes a liberty with its front page.
explanation.definitionFit: A banal, overused remark is a trite saying, a commonplace used as a noun.

clue.text: Records showing the man's right?

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
the Tories, Britain's Conservatives, are the political right

explanation.surface: Asking whether documents prove a man was in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are the members of Britain's Conservative Party, the right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Written accounts of past events are chronicles or records.

clue.text: Human being upset prophet

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the word human are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A distressed person who happens to be a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human being' looks like one phrase, but 'being' only links fodder and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Friendly inquiry about my competence

explanation.surface: A cordial person asking whether they are up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is split as a question: 'Am I able?'
explanation.definitionFit: Genial and good-natured means friendly; split as three words the letters ask whether I am capable.

clue.text: Dealing in, say. French and German imports

definitions.text: Dealing in, say. French and German imports

parts.words: Dealing in, say. French and German imports
parts.note: dealing in means handling a language, not trading: a person able to use both of two tongues, such as French and German

explanation.surface: A trader importing goods from France and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a trader; the sense is someone fluent in two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking two languages fluently, as a trader with France and Germany might need.

clue.text: Ruler having another spell in Golden State shortly

indicators.note: having another spelling says one sound is written a different way, the F sound becoming PH

parts.note: California is the Golden State, and Calif is its short form

explanation.surface: A ruler spending another stint living in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of time, but means spelling: CALIF and CALIPH are variant spellings of the same title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Muslim civil and religious leader, successor to Muhammad, so a ruler.

clue.text: Shoots lots of animals in parts of China

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
herds are large groups of animals

explanation.surface: A hunter shooting herds in parts of China the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is porcelain, and the pieces are broken fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken fragments of pottery, as found on archaeological digs, are pieces of china.

clue.text: Host upset an agricultural worker

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for host is turned upside down

parts.note: a host is a multitude, a myriad

explanation.surface: An upset host proves to be a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MYRIAD into DAIRYM; 'Host' is a great number, not a party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who works in or runs a dairy, milking cows, is a farm worker.

clue.text: Film director and writer, say

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the writer's name and listen to how it sounds

parts.note: H. G. Wells was the English writer of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: Naming someone who both directs films and writes.
explanation.walkthrough: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane and broadcast Wells's The War of the Worlds on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles made Citizen Kane, among the most famous films ever directed.

clue.text: Moderate start to season, frequently

indicators.note: start to picks out the opening letter of the word season

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: A mild start to a season that occurs often.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to temper or make it less harsh.

clue.text: Sort of table with drink on it for evening consumption

parts.note: a high table is the raised table for dons at a college dinner
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A kind of table with a beverage set on it for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH TEA is a British early-evening meal with tea and cooked food.
explanation.definitionFit: An early-evening meal with tea and hot food is something eaten at dusk.

clue.text: Friend of prince whose ration is pointless

indicators.note: pointless means the compass points W, S, E and N are all taken out of the words

explanation.surface: A prince's companion who gets no point from his allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes W, S, E and N, the four compass points, from WHOSE RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal companion in Shakespeare's play about the Danish prince.

clue.text: Falling from Big Ben when drunk

indicators.note: when drunk says the letters of Big Ben stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone toppling from the London clock tower after a drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great bell of the clock tower at Westminster in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing describes a tide going out or something dwindling, so declining.

clue.text: Pro-Greek fighter landed in Notts

parts.note: a lord with an estate in Nottinghamshire who went to fight for Greek independence; landed means owning land, not arriving

explanation.surface: A soldier for Greece coming ashore in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county; the poet held Newstead Abbey there and died in Greece in 1824 supporting its war of independence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet was a landed peer in Nottinghamshire who joined the Greek struggle against Ottoman rule.

clue.text: Fleet Street contains an awful mixture of printers

indicators.note: contains says the street abbreviation holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: RD, road, stands in for street
pi or pie is printers' term for a jumbled heap of type

explanation.surface: Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district, holds a mess of printers.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the London home of the newspapers; 'Fleet' alone is the definition, meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift, quick on one's feet.

clue.text: Collect together in order to get tuck

parts.note: for can mean in order to, as in 'go for a walk'
a tuck and a gather are both folds sewn into fabric

explanation.surface: Gathering people to get some food, tuck being schoolboy slang for snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for sweets and snacks, but here it is a sewing fold.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgather is to assemble or meet, an old word for gathering as a group.

clue.text: Wooden pale

explanation.surface: A wooden fence post, a pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like a stake in the fence, but it means wan.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of ash timber, so of wood; and grey-faced with shock, as in going white.

clue.text: Reckless forward, outside right

indicators.note: outside says the word for forward is wrapped around the letter for right

parts.note: forward in the sense of cheeky or impudent

explanation.surface: A rash forward player out on the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' and 'outside right' suggest football positions; they are cheeky and an instruction to place R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking prudence or caution, acting rashly, means much the same as reckless.

clue.text: Women — not all, though, are married

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that only some women are wed.
explanation.definitionFit: The wives and concubines of a household, kept in their own quarters, form a group of women.

clue.text: Israeli tribe knowing it may annoy Arabs

parts.note: Gad is one of the twelve tribes of Israel
fly is slang for knowing or shrewd

explanation.surface: A shrewd tribe of Israel that irritates Arab people.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs are not people but the horse breed, which biting flies torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting insect that pesters horses and cattle, and Arab horses are among its victims.

clue.text: Hanky-panky for working lad

parts.note: going means functioning or working, as a machine is going
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: Mischief standing in for a lad with a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or suspicious behaviour, shenanigans, is what hanky-panky means.
